key_insight: Carefully designed, parameter-efficient self-supervised adaptation of image-pretrained models can add temporal dynamics for video while preserving inter-video semantic separability, achieving stable and discriminative video representations without heavy fine-tuning.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between static image pretraining and dynamic video tasks by resolving the trade-off where heavy fine-tuning hurts inter-video semantic separability and overly few tunable parameters harm intra-video temporal consistency.
method: Introduce lightweight temporal adapters (dynamic modules) that inject temporal modeling into image-pretrained backbones with minimal additional parameters.

Combine complementary self-supervised objectives: an inter-video contrastive/separability loss to keep different videos distinguishable, and an intra-video temporal-consistency loss to stabilize representations across frames.
Adopt a selective, parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy (e.g., temporal-only updates or adapter tuning) to balance efficiency and representation quality.
impact: Enables practitioners to repurpose large image models for video tasks more efficiently—reducing compute and annotation needs—while maintaining both discriminative power across videos and temporal stability within videos.

paper_title: From Static to Dynamic: Exploring Self-supervised Image-to-Video Representation Transfer Learning
paper_authors: Yang Liu, Qianqian Xu, Peisong Wen, Siran Dai, Xilin Zhao
